newsitem.title: SPAIN: S&P revises Santander outlook after acquisition.
newsitem.headline: S&P revises Santander outlook after acquisition.

text.p: U.S. rating agency Standard & Poor's said on Wednesday it revised Spain's Banco Santander rating outlook to negative from stable after its latest acquisition of a 35 percent stake in Argentinian bank Banco del Rio de La Pata.
S&P said it affirmed AA-minus long-term debt rating and A-1 plus short-term debt.

On Tuesday, Santander announced it would take control of Argentine Banco Rio de la Plata SA, with 51 percent of the voting rights, acquiring 35.06 percent of its share capital and an option for an additional 15 percent.
S&P added in its statement that Santander has an exposure in Latam of more $3.0 billion, which is more than half of its shareholders' equity.
These investments are coherent with the Santander strategy of diversification outside its domestic market, but the group increased its exposure in the Latam region.
Banco Rio de la Plata's ratings are BBB minus long term, and A-3 short term.
